name: dot-morph
title: Dot Morph
description: A menu dot that splits into three on hover with a gooey neck, then spins and blooms into a three-piece mark on press, with motion blur. Pass your own mark.
label: Playground by Petar Cirkovic
author: Petar Cirkovic <https://pettar.com>
attribution: playground, Copyright (c) 2026 Petar Cirkovic. MIT License.

props.name: size
props.description: Pixels per unit of the 24-unit icon grid (16 draws a 384 px icon). Whole numbers keep edges on the pixel grid.

props.name: mark
props.description: Three closed SVG paths (24-unit viewBox: top, lower left, lower right) around a core circle of radius 3.

props.name: colors
props.description: Hex colors the pieces, then the core, bloom into. Unset: one solid currentColor.

props.name: spin / twist / expandAt / duration
props.description: Orbit degrees, extra per-piece rotation lag, when the dots start to bloom (fraction of the morph), and morph length in ms.

props.name: splitDuration / goo
props.description: Split length in ms, and how gooey the split is (0 turns it off).

props.name: shutter / soften
props.description: Motion blur shutter angle (0 turns it off) and the extra soft blur at peak speed.

props.name: direction / speed
props.description: Orbit direction (1 clockwise) and a playback speed multiplier.

props.name: autoplay
props.description: Walk the loop on its own: dot, dots, mark, dots, dot.

props.name: labels
props.default: { toMark: "Show the mark", toDots: "Back to the menu dots" }
props.description: Accessible names, by what the next press does.

props.name: onStageChange
props.description: Called when the icon starts a step toward a new stage.

props.name: ...props
props.description: Native button attributes (className goes on the button).

a11y: A native button with aria-pressed: Enter and Space toggle the mark, and the accessible name says what the next press does.
Keyboard parity with hover: focusing it with the keyboard splits the dot, and leaving walks it home (a Labs addition).
The drawing is aria-hidden; focus is visible with a two-pixel ring.
Under prefers-reduced-motion every step jumps to its resting frame, with no spin, blur or goo.
